_comment: Same transfer as text_rebase_t5base_t5large_theseus_nearestmean.json (A=google/t5-v1_1-base -> B=google/t5-v1_1-large), method=steer_text instead of theseus. steer_text never writes B's backbone weights -- it fits a feature-space correction and adds it at eval time -- so B's backbone is identical (pretrained, untouched) for both the target_zeroshot baseline and the corrected condition. This avoids the head/backbone-consistency issue theseus has here: the nearest-mean head for B is built once on B's pretrained backbone, and that backbone never changes under steer_text, so the same head is always evaluated against the state it was calibrated on.
_source_head: Unlike the theseus config, source_task_heads is NOT set here on purpose: A's tuned_ckpts (a 'full' checkpoint) already contains A's real fine-tuned classification_head.* weights, which align_to_base_keys loads automatically when the checkpoint is read -- steer_text.prepare() reads w_a straight off that live head. Set source_task_heads explicitly only if A's checkpoint format does NOT already include head weights (e.g. a head-only or peft-adapter checkpoint).
_block_ridge_note: feature_regime=linear + stage_2_strategy=block_ridge directly exercises the depth-mismatch handling theseus doesn't have: B's 24 residual blocks get grouped down (block_group_strategy=concat) to match A's 12, so every one of B's blocks participates in the fit, not just a name-matching prefix. The forward-mode jvp this needs is linearizing A (t5-v1_1-base, ~220M params, 12 layers), NOT B -- affordable, well under steer_text's own 500M-parameter warning threshold. If this is too slow/memory-heavy on your allocation, fall back to feature_regime=standard + stage_2_strategy=global_ridge (see configs/text_rebase_t5_steer.json), which is architecture-mismatch-agnostic but does not use per-block correspondence at all.
